page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.114-456 is a flexible virtual machine instance engineered for high-concurrency computation. The hardware foundation consists of AMD EPYC 7742 processors operating on the x86_64 architecture at a base clock speed of 2.25 GHz. It provisions 114 dedicated physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled, supplying 228 vCPUs to the host environment. The instance features 456 GB of system RAM, maintaining an exact allocation profile of 2.0 GB of memory per core.

The physical host architecture focuses entirely on general and compute processing without bundled local storage or hardware accelerators. Because local storage is absent, all persistent operational disks and logging facilities must be attached via remote block storage volumes. The virtual machine includes no GPUs and relies strictly on CPU-bound execution. Inbound and outbound networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for connectivity.

The dedicated resource model provides predictable performance for workloads scaling across dozens of worker threads. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers cost efficiency for compute-intensive scenarios that do not demand extensive memory footprints. This profile aligns VM.Standard.E3.Flex.114-456 with parallel batch jobs, large-scale continuous integration workers, video transcoding queues, distributed analytics nodes, and high-throughput application servers.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.114-456 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance powered by AMD EPYC 7742 processors running at 2.25 GHz. Based on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 114 dedicated physical cores and 228 vCPUs with two threads per core. System memory is sized at 456 GB, resulting in a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes no local NVMe storage and contains zero GPUs, necessitating external network-attached volumes for data retention. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is provided for network interfacing. This high-density core configuration is built to handle heavily multithreaded workloads that require predictable CPU cycles, including automated CI/CD pipelines, large compilation jobs, batch execution frameworks, and distributed web serving tiers.
